response.title: what power station can run a computer
response.answer:
Yes. A portable power station can run a computer, including a laptop, desktop PC, gaming PC, and monitor.

The right power station depends on two things:

Power output (W): How much electricity your computer needs while running.

Battery capacity (Wh): How many hours the power station can keep it running.

What size power station do you need?

markup:
Yes. A **portable power station** can run a computer, including a laptop, desktop PC, gaming PC, and monitor.

The right power station depends on two things:

1. **Power output (W):** How much electricity your computer needs while running.
2. **Battery capacity (Wh):** How many hours the power station can keep it running.

## What size power station do you need?

| Computer type | Typical power usage | Recommended battery |
|---|---:|---:|
| Laptop | 30–100W | 300–500Wh |
| Office desktop + monitor | 100–250W | 500–1,000Wh |
| Gaming PC + monitor | 300–650W | 1,000–2,000Wh |
| High-end workstation | 500–1,000W+ | 2,000Wh+ |

These are approximate operating loads, not the computer's power supply rating. For a desktop, the station's continuous AC output must exceed the actual combined power draw, with some headroom.

## Recommended power stations

  <row align="center" justify="between">

    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{watts}W</title>

  <slider min={50} max={1000} step={25} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <label>Battery capacity</label>
  <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
    <radio value="512">512Wh</radio>
    <radio value="1024">1,024Wh</radio>
    <radio value="2048">2,048Wh</radio>
  </radio-group>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated running time</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(Number(capacity)*0.85/watts).toFixed(1)} hours</title>
    <caption>Approximate; actual runtime varies with load and inverter losses.</caption>
  </box>
</box>

One important consideration: if you need your computer to stay on during a power outage without restarting, check UPS transfer compatibility. A dedicated computer UPS is often the safer choice for uninterrupted operation.

**Two questions so I can recommend the right size:**

1. Is it a **desktop PC, gaming PC, or laptop**?
2. How many hours do you want to run it without electricity?
